neighbours.label: how a physical quantity varies in science prose ('varies linearly', 'depends on the temperature')
fire: The resistance of the wire increases linearly with its length.
The rate of the reaction depends strongly on the temperature of the solution.
In this range the stress grows linearly with the applied strain.
Crystal growth is controlled mainly by the pressure and temperature of the melt.
The signal strength falls off exponentially with distance from the source.
The solubility of the salt varies with temperature and the acidity of the water.
The deflection of the beam scales linearly with the load at the centre.
Equilibrium is generally reached within a few minutes at room temperature.
quiet: The wire is made of copper and coated in a thin layer of plastic.
The solution was stored in a brown glass bottle on the top shelf.
In this experiment the samples were cut from a single steel plate.
The crystals were collected and photographed under a microscope.
The signal was recorded by three antennas placed on the roof.
The salt was bought from a supplier in Germany and kept dry.
The beam was painted grey and bolted to the wall at both ends.
The lab is on the second floor and has two large windows.

notes: Card: peaks on 'ly' in 'varies linearly', ' temperature' in 'pressure and temperature' / 'depends on the temperature', ' generally' in 'is generally achieved', ' being' in 'are being felt'. Probe: 'varies linearly' 0.62, 'decreases as temperature rises' 0.17, non-science control 0.00. Near misses keep science prose but state static facts.
